description: Sir Edward Victor Appleton (6 September 1892 – 21 April 1965) was a British physicist who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1947 for his contributions to the knowledge of the ionosphere, which led to the development of radar and shortwave radio. A graduate of the University of Cambridge, Appleton was commissioned as a second lieutenant in the Royal Engineers in 1915.
